claims.claim: Spathis's text-mining comparison of four best-selling series reports that A Song of Ice and Fire lacks -ly adverbs relative to the other three series.
claims.quote: the lack of -ly adverbs in Game of Thrones

claims.claim: Spathis's key-takeaway list states that Game of Thrones contains significantly fewer -ly adverbs than the other series analysed.
Spathis's adverb finding is stated only for the -ly suffixed form of the adverb, never for adverbs as a whole class.
Spathis reports no numeric adverb rate in the article's running text; the adverb comparison is carried entirely by a chart image.
Spathis removed character names, along with very frequent words and phrases, as stopwords before ranking parts of speech.
Spathis's corpus is 3,896,568 words drawn from nineteen books by four authors.
Spathis's Automated Readability Index result places Game of Thrones at the comprehension level of 11-year-olds.
Spathis reports that Martin's most frequent colour adjectives across the series are red, white and grey.
claims.quote: Notable is the usage of colors by author
